newsitem.title: USA: Portland, Enron open to competition.
newsitem.headline: Portland, Enron open to competition.

text.p: Portland General Corp and Enron Corp said on Monday they have committed to submitting a plan to the Oregon Public Utility Commission within 60 days of the merger of the two firms to open Portland General Electric's market to competition.
The plan would allow residential, commercial and industrial customers to choose their energy provider.
"This commitment reflects our long-standing position that competition will be good for all of our customers," says Portland General Electric Chairman Ken Harrison.

The plan will include a proposal to separate PGE's generating facilities from its transmission and distribution system allowing customers to pay for the delivery of electricity separately from the electricity itself.
Enron and Portland General have agreed to merger in a tax-free stock-for-stock deal valued at about $2.1 billion. Shareholders have approved the merger which is pending regulatory approvals.
